title: Compilers: Course Notes
note: This PDF holds only the opening of the notes: the table of contents runs to section 4.12 on page 72, but the file stops early in chapter 4. Summaries are in our own words; the text stays in the PDF.
summary: A hands-on compilers course in which students build, in OCaml, a compiler from Tiger′ (a Pascal-like language with nested functions) to real x86-64 machine code that runs on their laptops. Kiselyov grows the compiler one language feature at a time, each step driven by tests written first, and builds it in tagless-final style: the source language is an OCaml signature, and interpreters, pretty-printers, transformations and the code generator are all just different implementations of it. The file covers the setup, what a compiler is, the tagless-final warm-up, and the first real step: compiling integer literals to assembly.
